citeAs: Clark, Peter, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, and Oyvind Tafjord. (2018). Think you have Solved Question Answering? Try ARC, the AI2 Reasoning Challenge.
creator: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, Oyvind Tafjord (Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence)
description: ARC is a dataset of 7,787 natural, non-diagram grade-school science multiple-choice questions authored for standardized tests, partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set. The release also includes the ARC Corpus of 14M science-related sentences and baseline models to support research on advanced question answering and reasoning.
name: AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC)
rai:dataBiases: The dataset design explicitly filters out questions answerable by simple retrieval or word co-occurrence methods by defining the Challenge Set as questions both baselines get wrong, in order to avoid scores being dominated by simple algorithms and the resulting research bias toward those methods. The authors also note the questions come from standardized tests authored for humans, which may include varying difficulty and design characteristics from those sources.
rai:dataCollection: The ARC dataset was assembled through several months of extensive search and investigation to obtain publicly releasable natural science questions authored for standardized tests. Questions were drawn from a variety of sources including state science assessments and an anonymous AI2 content partner, then partitioned into Challenge and Easy sets using two baseline solvers; the accompanying ARC Corpus was mined from the web using automatically constructed science-related queries based on hand-written templates and then augmented with AristoMini.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consist of natural, non-diagram grade-school science multiple-choice questions authored for standardized tests and drawn from sources such as state assessment programs, NAEP, TIMSS, and an anonymous AI2 content partner. For the ARC Corpus, raw data were web documents returned by science-related search queries before text extraction and sentence chunking.
rai:dataCollectionType: Document analysis, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that the Challenge/Easy split only approximates the informal goal of identifying hard questions because it is defined operationally by failure of two baseline solvers. The ARC Corpus contains relevant knowledge for many questions, but simple retrieval methods often cannot exploit it, and some required commonsense may remain unstated. The dataset is limited to non-diagram multiple-choice science questions from grades 3 to 9.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: After collection, questions were partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set based on whether both an information-retrieval solver and a PMI co-occurrence solver answered them incorrectly. For the ARC Corpus, collected web documents were de-duplicated, stripped down to text, chunked into sentences, and augmented with the AristoMini corpus.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For the question dataset, the authors filtered to natural science, non-diagram, multiple-choice questions and partitioned them into train/dev/test splits and Challenge/Easy subsets. For the ARC Corpus, web search results were collected, de-duplicated, stripped to text, and chunked into sentences; the corpus was then augmented with AristoMini.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended to encourage AI research in advanced question answering, reasoning, and science QA, and to provide a benchmark and leaderboard for the community. The ARC Corpus is provided as optional supporting knowledge for corpus-based approaches to the challenge.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Automated tools were used in dataset construction and filtering, including an Elasticsearch-based information retrieval solver, a PMI-based solver, a major search engine for collecting corpus documents, and Open IE in the released DGEM-OpenIE baseline pipeline.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: questions are sourced from standardized tests; the paper does not describe multiple independent annotations per item.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: no demographics of question authors, annotators, or reviewers are provided.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: no inter-annotator agreement or annotation quality metrics are reported for the dataset labels.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: no annotation platform is described; questions were collected from existing standardized tests rather than crowd annotation.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: the paper does not describe a human labeling protocol for creating question-answer annotations beyond sourcing existing multiple-choice science questions.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: the paper does not discuss missing records, incomplete items, or missing observations in the dataset.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: no collection date range or period for gathering the questions or corpus is stated.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: no imputation or fill-in strategy for missing values is described.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: no versioning, update cadence, or maintenance commitment is described.
null_reasons.rai:dataSocialImpact: the paper does not explicitly discuss broader social or ethical impacts of releasing the dataset.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: the paper describes science exam questions and corpus sentences, and does not indicate collection of personal or sensitive information.
